facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus lived approximately 73 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous.
facts.quote: Naashoibitosaurus (from Navajo —"creek lizard") is a genus of hadrosaurid dinosaur that lived about 73 million years ago

facts.statement: Fossils of Naashoibitosaurus were found in the Kirtland Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.
facts.quote: and was found in the Kirtland Formation of the San Juan Basin in New Mexico, United States.

facts.statement: To date, only a partial skeleton of Naashoibitosaurus has been discovered.
facts.quote: Only a partial skeleton has been found to date.

facts.statement: Jack Horner first described the type specimen of Naashoibitosaurus as belonging to the genus Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: It was first described as a specimen of Kritosaurus by Jack Horner

facts.statement: David Gillette and David Thomas collected the type specimen, believing it came from the Naashoibito Member of the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: David Gillette and David Thomas collected the type and only known specimen from what was thought to be the Naashoibito Member of the Kirtland Formation

facts.statement: The specimen was actually collected from the older, late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member, not the Naashoibito Member.
facts.quote: Instead, it came from the older, late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member.

facts.statement: In 1992, Jack Horner described the skull as belonging to an immature Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Horner described the skull in 1992 as that of an immature Kritosaurus

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas initially described the postcranial bones as belonging to Edmontosaurus saskatchewanensis.
facts.quote: Hunt and Lucas were describing the postcrania as belonging to Edmontosaurus saskatchewanensis.

facts.statement: Hunt and Lucas assigned the specimen its own generic name, Naashoibitosaurus, after realizing the skull did not match Edmontosaurus and Kritosaurus was indeterminate.
facts.quote: When the disconnect became apparent, Hunt and Lucas gave the specimen its own generic name

facts.statement: Thomas Williamson challenged the separation of Naashoibitosaurus and Kritosaurus in 2000.
facts.quote: Their assessment was challenged in 2000 by Thomas Williamson

facts.statement: Thomas Williamson supported Horner's argument that nasal crests in hadrosaurines move backward on the skull during growth.
facts.quote: He returned to Horner's argument, noting as Horner had that the nasal crest in other hadrosaurines like Prosaurolophus moves back on the skull during growth.

facts.statement: A 2014 study concluded that while Naashoibitosaurus is similar to Kritosaurus, it represents a distinct species.
facts.quote: A 2014 study agreed with previous authors that Naashoibitosaurus is similar to Kritosaurus, but found it to be a distinct species.

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus is classified as a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a type of flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill dinosaur.
facts.quote: Naashoibitosaurus is a saurolophine hadrosaurid, a "flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill".

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus is most closely related to solid-crested hadrosaurids like Saurolophus.
facts.quote: It is closest to the solid-crested forms like Saurolophus.

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus belongs to the subfamily Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: subfamilia: Saurolophinae

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus was a large herbivore capable of moving on two or four legs.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Naashoibitosaurus would have been a large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus had continuously replacing teeth packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any given time.
facts.quote: Its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus used a broad beak to crop plants and cheek-like organs to hold food in its jaws.
facts.quote: Plant material would have been cropped by its broad beak, and held in the jaws by a cheek-like organ.

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus could feed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters (13 feet) high.
facts.quote: Feeding would have been from the ground up to ~4 meters (13 ft) above.

facts.statement: Naashoibitosaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous, specifically the Campanian stage, approximately 73 million years ago.
facts.quote: vivió a finales del período Cretácico, en el Campaniense, hace aproximadamente entre 73 millones de años

facts.statement: The time range for Naashoibitosaurus is estimated from 83.6 to 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: Its skull, the most thoroughly described portion, has a low nasal crest that peaks in front of the eyes, but does not strongly arch as in Gryposaurus.
